articleHeadline: Cryo-EM Reveals How FMDV O/Cathay Variants Evade Neutralizing Antibodies
articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) O/Cathay topotype circulating in East and Southeast Asia shows antigenic drift that reduces neutralization by infection- and vaccine-induced antibodies. articleSummary: Tuberculosis remains a global threat, with 2023 reporting 8.2 million new cases and 1.25 million deaths; about 400,000 MDR/RR-TB cases worldwide, only 44% diagnosed and treated. Management suggests collecting fish smaller than 10 cm during cooler months to exploit lower transmission. Epidemiological metrics used include prevalence, mean intensity, mean abundance, and mean crowding to describe aggregation and inform targeted removal of heavily infected hosts.

articleHeadline: Australia launches dengue vaccine; two doses cost AU$300, please note vaccination guidelines.
articleSummary: Australia launches dengue vaccine Qdenga; two-dose course costs AU$300 (AU$150 per dose), with doses spaced three months apart. articleSummary: Bangkok, Thailand—199 pregnant women at Rajavithi Hospital were followed during 2021-2022. articleHeadline: Liver abscess due to bacteria.

articleHeadline: A One-Dollar Bedside Test Catches Deadly Superbugs in Rural Hospitals
articleSummary: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) carriage detected at the bedside in a Vietnamese ICU (Viet Tiep Hospital) using pre-formulated chromogenic agar plates and a portable incubator, performed by nurses for under $1 per test. articleHeadline: From AI X-Rays to Ultra-Short Drug Regimens: 2025's Tuberculosis
articleSummary: Tuberculosis remains a leading killer, with global incidence falling about 1.5–2% annually and still short of WHO End TB 2030 targets. A Frontiers in TB narrative synthesis of 2025 notes rapid progress in diagnostics, therapeutics, vaccines, and care, yet health-system gaps constrain impact. In diagnostics, AI-assisted chest radiography improved sensitivity and reader consistency in high-volume screening across India and Southeast Asia, with pooled sensitivity often above 85%. Nigeria demonstrated cost-effective use of ultraportable X-ray with AI interpretation. Tongue-swab PCR (SMART4TB) in Philippines, South Africa, Nigeria, and Zambia yielded specificity 99.6% and sensitivity 66% versus culture, best used within diagnostic algorithms. Stool-based GeneXpert Ultra testing matured, showing robust performance despite stool variability and improved pediatric confirmation. WHO guidance urged concurrent multi-specimen testing in children, including stool, respiratory samples, and urine LAM for HIV-positive children. Therapeutics moved to shorter regimens: a four-month all-oral rifapentine–moxifloxacin–isoniazid–pyrazinamide regimen was noninferior to six months (Study 31).
